I hope all is well with you. I have made some progress internally and believe we are ready to move forward if you will reasonably understand our position better.

BNY appreciates LSEG’s engagement and remains committed to closing this matter promptly and on commercially reasonable terms. We outline below a practical path to resolution that addresses the period when LSEG first specifically raised the NAV‑calculation use case with BNY and that sets us up correctly on a go‑forward basis.

Framework to resolve the past claim

-          Look‑back window. BNY is prepared to resolve any past‑period exposure from April 1, 2023 through the effective date of a new agreement. We will not agree to retroactive fees prior to that point. 

 This is the time LSEG first directly engaged BNY’s market‑data sourcing team on the relevant use case (third‑party NAVs) and sought to align licensing. Before that, LSEG had not provided a targeted, effective notice to the appropriate BNY stakeholders identifying the specific use case or any change to the status quo. 

-          Commercial approach. Within that limited period, BNY is prepared to reasonably accommodate the applicable “Derived Data – other than Indices/Benchmarks” license fees (with the correct end‑customer banding), net of any overlapping rights already paid for, and recognizing that Derived Data does not attract Data Charges where the appropriate license is held.

-          Release of earlier claims. In exchange, LSEG will confirm in writing that it waives and releases any claim for back fees or charges for any period prior to April 1, 2023.

This structure is equitable and consistent with the parties’ course of dealing. From 2019 on, BNY operated in good‑faith reliance on existing Order Forms and longstanding disclosures of our fund‑administration activities. LSEG’s 2018 “policy and commercial model” communication was generic and contemplated follow‑up to “walk through” changes; however, no direct, targeted engagement with the appropriate BNY sourcing/legal contacts occurred until well into 2023. Had BNY been specifically notified earlier, they may have been able to mitigate the extra expense, either by adjusting usage and/or contractually passing through incremental costs to affected clients. Those responses to the LSEG change are no longer feasible years later.

 

Go‑forward alignment

-          License. BNY will in good faith review, negotiate and enter in to the “Calculation and Distribution of Derived Data other than Indices/Benchmarks” license covering NAV calculation on behalf of third parties and any other applicable Derived Data uses, with the correct banding and entities listed on the Order Form.

-          Operational governance. Upon execution, BNY will implement the required reporting and governance under LSEG’s policies and will work with your team to ensure that our disclosures, end‑customer counts (if applicable), and any technical controls fully align with the policy framework.

 

Next steps

If the above framework is acceptable, please schedule some time to discuss with me the going-forward draft order form and a settlement letter reflecting: (i) fees for the period April 1, 2023–present, (ii) a mutual reservation of rights prospectively until execution, and (iii) LSEG’s waiver/release for all periods pre‑April 1, 2023. We can then confirm banding and finish the paperwork.

 

We value our relationship with LSEG and would like to close this matter swiftly on terms that are principled, fair, and proportionate. Please let me know your availability to discuss.
